summary.text: A 37-year-old woman was hospitalized at a local hospital for hemorrhoids and underwent PPH with injection sclerotherapy. On the fourth postoperative day a rectovaginal fistula was found with vaginal discharge, fecal discharge and bloody purulent secretions. She had transvaginal fistula resection with layered suture repair and levofloxacin, but three days later bloody purulent secretions and fecal discharge persisted, and she was transferred to the authors' hospital.

Laboratory tests showed white blood cells 12 × 10^(9)/L, neutrophils 9.6 × 10^(9)/L, C-reactive protein 126 mg/L and procalcitonin 1.26 ng/mL, read by the authors as constant infection and inflammation; rectal CT showed no obvious fistula. Prophylactic ileostomy, fecal diversion and a cephalosporin antibiotic followed; after 7 days fecal outflow persisted, and endoscopy showed a failed repair, a roughly 10 mm rectal fistula about 5 cm from the anus, a connected vaginal fistula, and no malignancy on biopsy.

Ileostomy and diversion were continued for 8 weeks until endoscopy judged the fistula ready for repair, although the sources describe the inflammation both as disappeared and as significantly relieved. A combined transanal and transvaginal endoscopic repair then used a hook knife mucosal pinhole, argon plasma coagulation and nylon loop-assisted through-the-scope clip purse-string closure of both fistula openings, with 24 clips and an operation time of 125 minutes.

She had no postoperative complications and was discharged on the seventh postoperative day. Endoscopy at 5 weeks showed a healing fistula site and another endoscopy 12 weeks later showed white scar-like mucosal changes at both sites, barium enema showed no contrast outside the rectal cavity, and gynecologic examination showed no fistula. The ileostomy was closed. At the 1-year follow-up she had no recurrence, no serious complication, no discomfort and normal sexual function.

ambiguities.issue: The reexamination after the continued diversion is described as the inflammation having disappeared in the abstract and results, but as the margin inflammation being significantly relieved with the fistula still visible in the case description.

evidence.quote: After 8 weeks, the endoscopic fistula inflammation disappeared
the mucosal inflammation at the margin of fistula was significantly relieved

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile disappeared and significantly relieved into one description.

ambiguities.issue: The interval to the endoscopic reexamination after ileostomy is 8 weeks in the text but the Figure 1E-H caption says 1 month after ileostomy; the text also says the diversion lasted 8 weeks (4 weeks as required).

evidence.quote: Eight weeks later, a reexamination of digestive endoscopy revealed
(E, F) Endoscopic manifestations of rectal fistula 1 month after ileostomy.
Preventive ileostomy and fecal diversion treatment were continued for 8 weeks (4 weeks as required)

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not choose one interval or compute a calendar date for the reexamination.

ambiguities.issue: The 12-week endoscopy is "12 weeks later" than the 5-week reexamination in the body text, but "After 12 weeks of surgery" in the abstract and "3 months after repairing operation" in the Figure 3 caption; the 5-week visit is "1 month" in the caption.

evidence.quote: Another endoscopic examination 12 weeks later revealed white scar-like changes
After 12 weeks of surgery, a follow-up endoscopic examination showed
(C) Endoscopic manifestations of rectal fistula 3 months after repairing operation.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide whether 12 weeks counts from the operation or from the 5-week visit.

ambiguities.issue: The 7-day treatment combines prophylactic ileostomy, fecal diversion and cephalosporin antibiotic; the antibiotic duration and drug name are not stated separately.

evidence.quote: combined treatment with cephalosporin antibiotics on the patient. However, after the 7-day treatment

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a 7-day duration or a specific cephalosporin to the antibiotic.

ambiguities.issue: "The infection status of the stoma was serious" does not say whether the stoma is the fistula orifice or the ileostomy (the text calls the fistula orifice a stoma elsewhere).

evidence.quote: the infection status of the stoma was serious
inflammation at the fistula stoma disappeared

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which stoma was infected or when.

article_limitations: Single case report; no calendar dates are given, so all times are literal relative phrases.
Text and figure captions give different intervals for the reexaminations (8 weeks versus 1 month after ileostomy; 12 weeks later versus 3 months after the repair); recorded as ambiguities.
Inflammation at the eight-week reexamination is described as disappeared and as significantly relieved; recorded as two review-only source-conflict facts.
Discussion sentences on the literature, success rates of other series and device choice are not recorded as patient facts.
Pixels are reviewed in the separate visual submission; Figure 3G and 3H show axial cross-sectional images although the caption calls them ileostomy status.
